mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-quarter increase in real GDP growth above 3% signals a robust demand-driven expansion, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: If real GDP growth exceeds 3% for four consecutive quarters but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the industrial production index below -1% signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: If industrial production declines by more than 1% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 4% for three consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 6% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
